title: Straighten the Tree Into a List

concept.title: Hang the left subtree between the root and the right subtree
body: Rearrange the nodes of a tree **in place** so that the tree becomes a chain: every node has no left child, and its right child is the next node in the **pre-order** walk of the original tree. For each node the new order is: the node, then the whole (flattened) left subtree, then the whole (flattened) right subtree.

A recursive function flattens a subtree and returns its **last node** (the tail of the chain). At a node: flatten both children, then move the left chain to the right side: `root.right = root.left`, `root.left = None`, and attach the old right chain to the **tail of the left chain**.

body.code:
def flatten(root):                       # returns the last node of the chain
    if root is None:
        return None
    left_tail = flatten(root.left)
    right_tail = flatten(root.right)
    if root.left is not None:
        left_tail.right = root.right         # the old right chain follows the left chain
        root.right = root.left
        root.left = None
    return right_tail or left_tail or root

body: The returned tail is the right tail if it exists, otherwise the left tail, otherwise the node itself. The printed result is a tree whose level-order form is `v1 N v2 N v3 ...`.

statement: Rearrange the nodes of a binary tree in place so that no node has a left child and the right child of every node is the next node in the pre-order walk of the original tree. Print the resulting tree in level order in the same form as a tree in the input (`N` for a missing child, no `N` at the end).
inputFormat: The first line has `t`, the number of words in the description of the tree.
The second line has the tree in level order: the root first, then the children of the nodes row by row from left to right. `N` stands for a missing child. There is no `N` at the end.
outputFormat: The flattened tree in level order on one line.
constraints: The height of the tree is at most 800.

examples.note: The pre-order is 1 2 3 4 5 6; the result is the chain 1 N 2 N 3 N 4 N 5 N 6.

hints: Flatten the left and the right subtree first.
Put the flattened left subtree in the place of the right subtree, and attach the old right subtree at its end.
Have the function return the last node of the chain, so that you can attach the old right chain to it.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


# Builds a binary tree from a level-order list of words; "N" marks a missing child.
def build_tree(vals):
    if not vals or vals[0] == "N":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1
    while head < len(queue) and i < len(vals):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if vals[i] != "N":
            node.left = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(vals) and vals[i] != "N":
            node.right = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root


# Prints a tree in the same level-order form ("empty" for no tree).
def print_tree(root):
    if root is None:
        print("empty")
        return
    out = []
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    while head < len(queue):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if node is None:
            out.append("N")
        else:
            out.append(str(node.val))
            queue.append(node.left)
            queue.append(node.right)
    while out and out[-1] == "N":
        out.pop()
    print(" ".join(out))


# Python in the browser cannot free a very long chain of nodes at once, and the result of this task is one long chain,
# so free_tree() (called at the end) cuts the links first and the nodes are then freed one by one.
def free_tree(root):
    stack = [root]
    while stack:
        node = stack.pop()
        for child in (node.left, node.right):
            if child is not None:
                stack.append(child)
        node.left = None
        node.right = None


def flatten(root):
    # Your code here: change the tree in place; return the last node of the chain
    return root

t = int(input())
vals = input().split()

root = build_tree(vals)
flatten(root)
print_tree(root)
free_tree(root)

explanation: Both subtrees are flattened first; then the left chain is moved to the right side and the old right chain is attached to the tail of the left chain. The function returns the tail of the whole chain.
